analyst_view.overall: OFI Crete (16th, 6 pts) host Anderlecht (15th, 6 pts) in Heraklion, a straight fight for a play-off place between two sides on two wins from four. OFI lost 2-0 at home to Panathinaikos and have a long injury list: Kenan Kodro (receiving treatment), Koutsoupias, Lagoudakis, Chnaris and Marinakis, with Aaron Iseka on an individual programme and Borja Gonzalez feeling his quadriceps; the numbers count the listed ones. Kresimir Krizmanic, listed out, took part in most of Tuesday's training, so he may be closer than the numbers assume. Anderlecht are without Lucas Hey and Ilay Camara (both counted), with Sikan and Cvetkovic expected up front, and travel despite a Greek general strike. Estonian referee Kristo Tohver, who has shown about 5.3 cards a game in his few matches on file, is in charge, which the numbers already count.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.4 goals and already take about 6% off OFI for Kodro and add about 6% to Anderlecht for Krizmanic missing at the back. Krizmanic training again could make that addition too big, but Borja Gonzalez's knock trims OFI's attack too, so with both still unconfirmed I stay at 2.4.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.6 corners, already up for OFI conceding many corners lately (35 in their last four). Anderlecht like the ball and press high, which the numbers already reflect, so I stay at 9.6.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.4 cards and already add about 11% for referee Kristo Tohver's high card count (5.3 a game in six matches). A tight game for a play-off place could add a booking, but that is what the numbers already assume, so I stay at 4.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.4 shots, already lower for OFI's thin recent shooting (28 in four) and higher for Anderlecht's. That matches OFI's injury-hit midfield, so I stay at 26.4.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.7 shots on target, already raised for Anderlecht against an OFI side that has allowed 33 on target in six. Without confirmed absences beyond what the numbers count, I stay at 9.7.
